# The RT64 shaders the web page builds: one shader description a line, other mode L and H, color combiner L and H,
# flags, in hex. RT64 specializes each one's WGSL when the page is built. In Chrome it builds the whole list behind the
# game from its first frame; in Firefox those above the first "section" line before the game starts, and a section when
# a frame first asks for 4 of its shaders, the game waiting. So nothing draws with the ubershader, which integrated
# graphics can't afford (N64Recomp-browser's README). A description in two sections is built with the first.
#
# Recorded by code, not by playing (the page's default settings): bash tools/record_shaders.sh (its header says how)
# runs N64Recomp-browser's tools/record_shaders.mjs with tools/shader_plan.json, which loads the page fresh for each
# test, and tools/shader_survey.js presses through the menus to the test and flies it for 12 s, banking both ways and
# climbing and diving. Above the first section: the launcher, the logos and the title screen, all Firefox waits for
# before the first frame. Then the menus up to a class overview; the attract demo the title screen plays when left
# alone; a section for each island and vehicle, what every test of that vehicle on that island drew, put together by
# tools/merge_shader_sections.py: every test of every class, the bonus vehicles too; and last the results screen,
# whose recording flies the cannonball's first test to reach it, so that its section holds only what the tests don't.
# Not recorded: the cannonball's later targets (its code resets the test itself), the photo album, the credits and
# the options screen. Most of the 12 s end in a crash or a landing, which draws the results. A shader the list misses
# is built behind the game, and the page remembers it and builds it with the rest on the next visit.
